$comment: Written by scripts/sync-workflow-engine.mjs (never by hand, except `coverage`, which the sync keeps as it finds it and scripts/test-workflow-engine.mjs holds to the upstream test list). docs/WORKFLOW_ENGINE.md says how to refresh. Where the upstream checkout lives is the operator's (WORKFLOW_ENGINE_SOURCE), never recorded here.
header: Vendored workflow engine: generated by scripts/sync-workflow-engine.mjs, never edited by hand. Source, commit and local patches: lib/workflow-engine/UPSTREAM.json

local_patches.import-specifiers: A relative import gains `.ts`, so the files load under node --experimental-strip-types (the mold's convention).
local_patches.erasable-syntax: TypeScript parameter properties (two, in balancer.ts and store.ts) become a field and an assignment on the same line; strip-only mode refuses a parameter property. Same behaviour.
local_patches.neutral-words: Whole comment lines (and the spec's title and $id lines) that named the upstream platform or company, an example taken from a client, or a line of business are replaced by neutral lines. The originals are not stored: each patch names its lines by sha256(salt + text), salt `neutral-words:`, and only a sync from the upstream checkout can apply it. No identifier or value that code reads changes (the three kept_identifiers stay as upstream spells them).

kept_identifiers.why: Entries of PLATFORM_USER_ATTRIBUTES: the directory fields the upstream platform sends with every user, which validateWorkflow lets a directory query name and refuses to see redeclared. Renaming them would change what the validator accepts, so they are kept as upstream spells them. The mold's people carry none of them; a later phase (people data) maps the mold's own fields.
